title: Swasthya Rakshak (Health, First Aid & Emergency)
description: Essential medical guidance: first aid, pediatric dosage guidelines, disease prevention, stroke/heart attack emergency, and public health schemes.

chunks.title: Pediatric Paracetamol Dosage Protocol
chunks.text: Paracetamol dosage for children is strictly weight-based: 10 to 15 mg per kg body weight per dose, administered every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum 4 doses (or 60 mg/kg) within 24 hours. Always use an oral dosing syringe, never a household teaspoon. Never combine with other multi-symptom cold medicines containing paracetamol.

chunks.title: Diarrhea & Dehydration ORS Preparation
chunks.text: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) is the cornerstone treatment for acute diarrhea. Dissolve 1 full WHO-formula ORS sachet into exactly 1 litre of clean boiled and cooled drinking water. Stir until completely dissolved. Give frequent small sips. Accompany with Zinc supplement tablets (20 mg daily for children >6 months, 10 mg for <6 months) for 14 continuous days.

chunks.title: First Aid for Burns & Scalds
chunks.text: Immediately immerse the burned area under cold, gentle running water for at least 20 minutes to halt thermal tissue destruction. Remove tight jewellery before swelling occurs. Cover loosely with sterile cling film or clean non-adherent cloth. DO NOT apply ice, toothpastes, turmeric, butter, or oil. Seek urgent medical attention if the burn exceeds the size of the victim's palm.

chunks.title: Dengue Warning Signs & Monitoring
chunks.text: Critical phase of Dengue occurs between days 3 and 7 when fever drops. Danger signs requiring immediate hospitalization: severe persistent abdominal pain, recurrent vomiting, bleeding gums or nose, mucosal hemorrhage, extreme lethargy, sudden drop in platelet count accompanied by rise in hematocrit. Avoid Aspirin and Ibuprofen; only use Paracetamol.

chunks.title: Adult Hands-Only CPR Protocol
chunks.text: If an adult collapses and is unresponsive and not breathing normally: 1. Call emergency services (112 / 108) immediately. 2. Position the heel of your hand on the centre of the patient's chest. 3. Push hard and fast at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute to a depth of 5-6 cm (about 2 inches). Allow complete chest recoil between each push.

chunks.title: Hypertension & Diabetes Dietary Management
chunks.text: Hypertension: Restrict dietary sodium to less than 2 grams per day (under 5 grams of table salt). Increase dietary potassium through bananas, green leafy vegetables, and lentils. Diabetes: Prioritize high-fiber complex carbohydrates (whole grains, millets), avoid refined sugars and sugary beverages, and engage in minimum 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise weekly.

chunks.title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY Scheme Details
chunks.text: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides cashless secondary and tertiary hospitalization cover of up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year across empaneled public and private hospitals across India. Covers pre-existing conditions from day one, including pre- and post-hospitalization expenses for up to 15 days.

chunks.title: Snakebite First Aid (Do's and Don'ts)
chunks.text: DO NOT tie tight tourniquets, do not suck venom, and do not make cuts on the bite mark. DO: Keep patient calm, immobilize the bitten limb using a splint or sling at heart level, remove rings and constrictive clothing, and rush immediately to a hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV). Polyvalent ASV neutralizes Cobra, Krait, Russell's Viper, and Saw-scaled Viper venoms.

chunks.title: Stroke Recognition (F.A.S.T. Protocol)
chunks.text: Recognize acute stroke using FAST: F (Face drooping on one side), A (Arm weakness when raising both arms), S (Speech difficulty, slurring, inability to repeat simple sentence), T (Time to call 108 immediately). Golden window for intravenous thrombolysis (tissue plasminogen activator tPA) is within 4.5 hours of symptom onset.

chunks.title: Heart Attack Emergency Action
chunks.text: Symptoms: Crushing central chest pain or heaviness lasting >10 minutes, radiating to left shoulder, jaw, back, accompanied by sweating, nausea, shortness of breath. Action: Have patient rest comfortably, call 108, give 300 mg soluble Aspirin/Disprin to chew immediately (unless allergic or actively bleeding), and prepare for CPR if responsiveness is lost.

chunks.title: Dog Bite & Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)
chunks.text: Immediately wash the animal bite wound thoroughly under vigorous running water with soap for at least 15 minutes. Apply povidone-iodine or alcohol. DO NOT stitch the wound primarily. Administer Anti-Rabies Vaccine (ARV) on Days 0, 3, 7, and 28. For Category III bites (broken skin or bleeding), Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG) must be infiltrated into the wound.

chunks.title: Tuberculosis (TB) Symptoms & Treatment (DOTS)
chunks.text: Suspect pulmonary TB if cough lasts >2 weeks, accompanied by fever in evening, night sweats, weight loss, and hemoptysis (blood in sputum). Diagnosis via Sputum smear microscopy and CBNAAT/GeneXpert. Government provides free 6-month Fixed-Dose Combination (FDC) treatment under National TB Elimination Program (NTEP) plus ₹500/month Nikshay Poshan financial aid.
